body:
I can profile the exemplar after all - the prepared data is in the repo - and I CANNOT REPRODUCE ~9 s/node. I measure 0.4 s/node on the same mask, radius, conditions and fit. bd-01KZYYQCR3D7NDZQN5DN53AHRC may be stale; I would re-validate before optimizing.

Setup matched 05-crossnobis-uncertainty.R exactly: read_vol on mask4_vt.nii.gz, neuroim2_volume_domain, neuroim2_searchlights at RADIUS_MM = 11.25, lm_relation_fit with sampling_unit='scan', fixed-identity noise_precision(diag(577)).

  features 577   centres 577   mean support 44.8   q = 8

MEASURED, JIT warmed, median of repeats:

  rdm_sampling_covariance(fixed_plan, fit, target='plugin')   0.314 - 0.414 s
  sampling_covariance() x2 including the transport query      0.141 s
  FULL LOOP BODY as 05 writes it                              0.455 s/node

At 0.455 s/node the full 577-centre sweep is about 4.4 minutes, not 90.

THE LEARNED-METRIC ARM IS NOT THE EXPLANATION - I checked that first, since it was my best guess. rdm_sampling_covariance on a crossnobis plan is refused outright: 'Analytic RDM sampling covariance is unavailable because this plan's neural metric was learned. Version 0.1 does not propagate metric-estimation uncertainty.' And plan_crossnobis builds in 1.2 s once, not per node.

PROFILE of the second call, JIT already warmed once: about 50 percent in cmpfun/genCode/tryInline - the byte-code compiler, i.e. still warm-up - and 22 percent in relation_fit_capabilities and .require_relation_fit_capability, i.e. validation. Neither is the covariance mathematics. grepl alone is 13.9 percent of self time.

WHAT I AM NOT SAYING: that the original measurement was wrong. I am saying it does not reproduce here against the current tree, and a twenty-fold gap is too large for machine variation. Either the figure predates a change that has since landed, or the original run measured conditions I have not reconstructed.

CHEAPEST NEXT STEP, before any optimization: re-run 05 as written and read its own node_seconds instrumentation. One run, no new code. If it now reports ~0.5 s/node the bead is resolved and the README Cost section needs an edit rather than the function needing a precompute-once object. If it still reports ~9 s while my direct reconstruction reports 0.455 s, then the cost is in something 05 does that I did not reproduce, and diffing the two scripts localizes it immediately.

Recording one verified-good separately: that refusal is exactly what the exemplar header promises the arm is for - 'the package declines to calibrate what it cannot calibrate, instead of returning a plausible number'. It does, and the message names the reason, the version limit, and two alternatives. That is the best refusal message I have seen in this package.
